version: RBI/DoS/2026-27/410; DoS.CO.CSITEG.4/31.01.015/2026-27 dated 31.07.2026 (Commercial Banks; effective on issue)

groups.title: Chapter I - Preliminary: B. Applicability

controls.title: Scope: Commercial Banks and the sibling 2026 Directions
controls.prose: The Directions apply to Commercial Banks, meaning banking companies other than Small Finance Banks, Payments Banks and Local Area Banks, corresponding new banks and the State Bank of India (Banking Regulation Act, 1949, section 5(c), (da) and (nc)). They are issued under sections 27 and 35-A of the BR Act and take effect immediately on issue (31 July 2026, paragraphs 1-2). On the same date RBI issued parallel Cybersecurity, Technology: Risk, Resilience and Assurance Framework Directions, 2026 for Small Finance Banks (RBI/DoS/2026-27/419), Payments Banks (RBI/DoS/2026-27/428), Urban Co-operative Banks (RBI/DoS/2026-27/437, four levels by digital depth), All India Financial Institutions (RBI/DoS/2026-27/456: EXIM Bank, NABARD, SIDBI, NHB, NaBFID), Non-Banking Financial Companies (RBI/DoS/2026-27/461, three requirement tiers: Base Layer below Rs 500 crore and Core Investment Companies, Base Layer Rs 500 crore and above, Middle Layer and above) and Credit Information Companies (RBI/DoS/2026-27/470).
controls.guidance: Catalog structure (no top-level structure field exists in the schema, so it is documented here): this catalog follows the paragraph numbering of the Commercial Banks Directions (RBI/DoS/2026-27/410, 233 paragraphs in eight chapters). Control ids are the bare paragraph number exactly as the instrument numbers it (e.g. 182 is DAKSH incident reporting, cited as rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026:182); paragraph numbers run 1-233 across the whole instrument, so they are unique without a chapter prefix. Paragraph 28 is split into 28 (CISO roles (1)-(5)), 28(6) (reporting line) and 28(7) (quarterly Board / RMCB / ITSC review) to match the sub-clauses the instruments registry cites. Group ids are 'Ch<n>.<section letter>' mirroring the instrument's section headings (Chapter VII has no lettered sections, so its group id is Ch7; the Z.1-Z.3 subsections of Chapter V section Z are Ch5.Z1-Ch5.Z3). In-text cross-references read 'para <n>' and name controls in this catalog. Definitions (paragraphs 5-6), commencement (1-2) and saving/interpretation (231-233) are folded into para 3 and para 230. Each control's guidance ends with the equivalent paragraph in each sibling Directions, found by text comparison of the RBI-published texts. Applicability: applicability.entityTypes lists the entity types whose own 2026 Directions carry the obligation and applicability.reCategories (present when NBFC layers or UCB levels narrow it) uses 'not-categorised' for banks, AIFIs and CICs, which RBI does not tier under these Directions. NBFC convention: the NBFC Directions have three requirement tiers (Base Layer below Rs 500 crore and Core Investment Companies; Base Layer Rs 500 crore and above; Middle Layer and above), but the reCategory vocabulary has a single nbfc-base-layer value. Wherever any Base Layer tier carries an obligation the control lists nbfc-base-layer together with the entity types nbfc, housing-finance-company and nbfc-p2p, and the guidance states the Rs 500 crore threshold where it applies, so a Base Layer entity below the threshold is recorded not-applicable with its asset size. NBFC-P2P platforms always remain in the Base Layer under the Scale Based Regulation, so they appear only on controls that bind the Base Layer. Tiers are not assumed to cascade: a control lists only the layers whose NBFC paragraph was found. HFCs follow the NBFC Directions by layer. Crosswalks to rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 are historical only: that Master Direction was repealed on 28 Nov 2025 and replaced by the entity-wise Managing Risks in Outsourcing Directions, 2025, which has no instrument id yet; new findings must cite this catalog first and the 2023 MD only as a secondary ref. Maxwell evidences scope by reading company-profile/<c>/details.json entityTypes and regulatoryRegistrations[].category during refresh-ctx and recording one soc control record per applicable control in refresh-soc. Regional Rural Banks and Local Area Banks are outside all seven Directions.
evidenceExpected: details.json entityTypes and RBI regulatoryRegistrations reviewed against the seven 2026 Directions
Applicability memo naming the sibling Directions that bind the company and, for NBFCs and UCBs, the layer or level relied on

controls.title: Foreign banks in branch mode: head office oversight and comply-or-explain
controls.prose: For a foreign bank operating in India through branches, references to the Board mean the controlling or head office overseeing Indian operations. Such a bank is subject to a comply-or-explain approach for Chapters II, III, IV and VII and for listed Chapter V paragraphs (49, 55, 62, 63, 64, 65, 89, 90, 92, 93, 95, 98, 104, 105, 110, 114, 126, 140, 141, 142, 151-155, 163-174, 175, 181, 183, 187, 190, 195 and 196); it may deviate from them only where RBI examines and accepts a reasonably justifiable explanation during supervision. Foreign banks may leverage controlling office, head office, regional or zonal committees for committee requirements as long as the governance obligations are met.
controls.guidance: Only relevant when details.json identifies a foreign bank branch. Keep a register of each paragraph where the bank explains rather than complies, the justification, the head-office control relied on and the RBI supervisory acceptance (inspection letter or RAR reference). Record deviations in the soc ledger as control records with a parameter pointing to the explanation, so refresh-soc does not raise findings RBI has already accepted.
evidenceExpected: Comply-or-explain register with RBI acceptance references
Head-office committee charters relied on for ITSC, ISC and ACB equivalents

groups.title: Chapter II - Role of the Board: A. Board Approved Policies

controls.title: Board approves IT, information asset, BCP, information security and cybersecurity strategies and policies
controls.prose: The Board of Directors must approve the bank's strategies and policies for Information Technology, Information Assets, Business Continuity, Information Security and Cybersecurity, including the Incident Response and Recovery Management / Cyber Crisis Management frameworks.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the Board resolution (date, agenda item, minutes extract) approving each named policy and strategy, and a policy register listing owner, version, approval date and next review. refresh-ctx records the register in company context; refresh-soc raises a finding when any of the six policy families lacks a Board approval, including an approved CCMP. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 6; Payments Bank Directions para 6; AIFI Directions para 6; Credit Information Company Directions para 6; NBFC Directions para 6 (all NBFCs, including NBFC-P2P platforms and HFCs in the Base Layer) and 68 (Middle Layer and above); UCB Directions para 7 (Level I and above).
evidenceExpected: Board resolutions approving IT, information asset, BCP, information security and cybersecurity strategies and policies
Policy register with approval dates and owners
Board-approved incident response and recovery / cyber crisis management framework

controls.title: Board reviews the strategies and policies at least annually
controls.prose: The strategies and policies approved under paragraph 7 must be placed before the Board for review at least once a year.
controls.guidance: Compare the last Board review date of each policy family with the retrieval date; more than 12 months since the last review is a gap. Store the review dates as soc control parameters so the next due date is computed from the catalog cadence. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 7; Payments Bank Directions para 7; AIFI Directions para 7; Credit Information Company Directions para 7; NBFC Directions para 69 (Middle Layer and above) and para 6 (all NBFCs including the Base Layer below Rs 500 crore, which is why nbfc-base-layer, HFCs and NBFC-P2P platforms are in applicability). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Board minutes showing annual review of each policy family
Policy review calendar

params.label: Maximum interval between Board reviews of the strategies and policies

groups.title: Chapter II - Role of the Board: B. Board Level Committees

controls.title: Board-level IT Strategy Committee constituted per Chapter III
controls.prose: The bank must have a Board-level IT Strategy Committee (ITSC) whose composition and functions follow paragraphs 16 to 19.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the Board resolution constituting the ITSC and its terms of reference cross-referencing paragraphs 16-19. The detailed composition and meeting tests are carried by paras 16-19; this control is satisfied when the committee exists with a Board-approved charter. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 8; Payments Bank Directions para 8; AIFI Directions para 8; Credit Information Company Directions para 8; NBFC Directions para 70. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Board resolution constituting the ITSC
ITSC terms of reference

controls.title: Audit Committee of the Board oversees IS Audit
controls.prose: The Audit Committee of the Board (ACB) is responsible for oversight of the bank's Information Systems (IS) Audit.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the ACB terms of reference naming IS Audit oversight and ACB minutes in which IS audit plans and reports were taken up. Detailed IS audit obligations are in paras 224-229. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 9; Payments Bank Directions para 9; AIFI Directions para 9; Credit Information Company Directions para 9; NBFC Directions para 149. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: ACB charter covering IS Audit oversight
ACB minutes reviewing IS audit plan and reports

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: A. IT Governance Framework

controls.title: IT governance focus areas
controls.prose: IT governance must focus on strategic alignment, risk management, resource management, performance management and Business Continuity / DR management.
controls.guidance: Check that the IT governance framework document (para 12) explicitly addresses all five focus areas; a missing area is a documentation gap of low severity. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 10; Payments Bank Directions para 10; AIFI Directions para 10; Credit Information Company Directions para 10; NBFC Directions para 65 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: IT governance framework mapping each of the five focus areas to owners and processes

controls.title: Robust IT governance framework with roles and oversight mechanisms
controls.prose: The bank must implement an IT Governance Framework built on the paragraph 11 focus areas that specifies the governance structure and processes needed to meet business and strategic objectives, the roles, authority and responsibilities of the Board, Board committees and Senior Management, and oversight mechanisms ensuring accountability and mitigation of IT and cyber / information security risks.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the Board-approved IT governance framework, a RACI covering Board, ITSC, IT Steering Committee, ISC, Head of IT and CISO, and the oversight reporting calendar. refresh-ctx captures the governance structure; gaps in role definition for any of these bodies are findings. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 11; Payments Bank Directions para 11; AIFI Directions para 11; Credit Information Company Directions para 11; NBFC Directions para 66 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: IT governance framework document
RACI for Board, committees and Senior Management
Oversight and escalation calendar

controls.title: Enterprise or operational risk policy assesses IT risks periodically
controls.prose: The enterprise-wide or operational risk management policy must also provide for periodic assessment of IT-related risks, both inherent and potential.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the ERM / ORM policy clause on IT risk assessment and the latest IT risk assessment report with inherent and residual ratings. Link risk records (rsk_) in the soc ledger to this control. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 12; Payments Bank Directions para 12; AIFI Directions para 12; Credit Information Company Directions para 12; NBFC Directions para 67 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: ERM or ORM policy clause covering IT risk
Most recent IT risk assessment with inherent and potential risk ratings

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: B. Information Security Policy and Cybersecurity Policy

controls.title: Information Security Policy content
controls.prose: The bank must have an Information Security Policy covering, among other things, its objectives, scope, ownership and responsibility, the information security organisation structure, exceptions, compliance review and penal measures for non-compliance.
controls.guidance: Document review of the Information Security Policy against the six listed elements; record which are missing. Exceptions handling should cross-reference the exception policy under para 59. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 13; Payments Bank Directions para 13; AIFI Directions para 13; Credit Information Company Directions para 13; NBFC Directions para 83 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
controls.category: Information Security Policy and Cybersecurity Policy
evidenceExpected: Approved Information Security Policy
Section mapping to objectives, scope, ownership, organisation, exceptions, compliance review and penal measures

controls.title: Distinct Board-approved Cybersecurity Policy
controls.prose: The bank must have a Board-approved Cybersecurity Policy setting out a strategy and approach to combat cyber threats suited to the complexity of its business and acceptable risk levels. It must be distinct and separate from the broader IT / Information Security policy so that cyber risks and mitigation measures are highlighted.
controls.guidance: Confirm a standalone cybersecurity policy document exists (not a chapter of the IT or IS policy), approved by the Board, with a cyber threat strategy and risk appetite statement. A cybersecurity section embedded in the IT policy is a finding. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 14; Payments Bank Directions para 14; AIFI Directions para 14; Credit Information Company Directions para 14; NBFC Directions para 84 (Middle Layer and above) and 22 (Base Layer Rs 500 crore and above); UCB Directions para 12 (Level I and above). Base Layer NBFCs, HFCs and NBFC-P2P platforms are in applicability because the NBFC Directions carry this obligation for the Base Layer tier of Rs 500 crore and above; a Base Layer entity below Rs 500 crore is out of scope for this control and should be recorded not-applicable with its asset size as the reason.
controls.category: Information Security Policy and Cybersecurity Policy
evidenceExpected: Standalone Board-approved Cybersecurity Policy
Board resolution approving it
Cyber risk appetite statement

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: C. IT Strategy Committee of the Board

controls.title: Establish a Board-level IT Strategy Committee
controls.prose: The bank must establish a Board-level IT Strategy Committee (ITSC).
controls.guidance: Evidence with the ITSC constitution resolution and current membership list. Where ITSC existed under the repealed 2023 IT Governance Master Direction, the prior approval continues to be governed by these Directions (paragraph 231). Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 15; Payments Bank Directions para 15; AIFI Directions para 15; Credit Information Company Directions para 15; NBFC Directions para 70 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
controls.category: IT Strategy Committee of the Board
evidenceExpected: Board resolution establishing the ITSC
Current ITSC membership

controls.title: ITSC composition: three directors, independent IT-expert chair, technically competent members
controls.prose: The ITSC must have at least three directors including its Chairperson. The Chairperson must be an independent director with substantial IT expertise, meaning at least seven years' experience managing information systems or leading / guiding technology or cybersecurity initiatives, and should understand the business processes and IT's impact on them. Members must be technically competent, able to understand and evaluate information systems and IT / cyber risks. Foreign bank branches may rely on controlling-office or regional committees if the governance obligations are met.
controls.guidance: Evidence with director profiles showing independence status and the Chairperson's seven-year IT / cybersecurity track record, plus a competence statement for each member. Record member count and chair experience as soc control parameters; fewer than three directors or a non-independent chair is a finding. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: NBFC Directions para 71. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
controls.category: IT Strategy Committee of the Board
evidenceExpected: ITSC membership list with independence status
Chairperson CV evidencing at least seven years of IT or cybersecurity leadership
Member technical competence assessment

params.label: Minimum number of directors on the ITSC including the Chairperson
Minimum IT experience of the independent director chairing the ITSC

controls.title: ITSC meets at least quarterly
controls.prose: The ITSC must meet at least once every quarter.
controls.guidance: Collect ITSC meeting dates for the last four quarters from minutes; a quarter without a meeting is a finding. Store the last meeting date so refresh-soc computes the next due date. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 17; Payments Bank Directions para 17; AIFI Directions para 17; Credit Information Company Directions para 17; NBFC Directions para 72 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
controls.category: IT Strategy Committee of the Board
evidenceExpected: ITSC minutes for each of the last four quarters
ITSC meeting calendar for the current financial year

params.label: Minimum ITSC meeting frequency

controls.title: ITSC functions: strategy, governance, risk, budget, escalation, BCP/DR review, capacity and access standards
controls.prose: The ITSC must: ensure an effective IT strategic planning process; guide preparation of an IT strategy aligned with the bank's overall strategy; satisfy itself that IT and information security governance fosters accountability, is effective and adequately resourced with clear responsibilities; ensure processes exist to assess and manage IT and cybersecurity risks; ensure IT and cybersecurity budgets are commensurate with IT maturity, digital depth, threat environment and industry standards and are used as intended; review organisational arrangements so security concerns are escalated for quick action; review at least annually the adequacy and effectiveness of BCP and DR management (limited to people, processes and systems for IT, IS and cybersecurity operations); review IT capacity assessments and remedial measures; and approve documented standards and procedures for need-based access to information systems.
controls.guidance: Map ITSC agenda items and minutes over the last 12 months to the nine functions; the annual BCP/DR adequacy review and the approval of need-based access standards are the most frequently missing and should each have a dated minute. Access standards approved here are the baseline runtime-probe-identity-access tests against. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 18; Payments Bank Directions para 18; AIFI Directions para 18; Credit Information Company Directions para 18; NBFC Directions para 73 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
controls.category: IT Strategy Committee of the Board
evidenceExpected: ITSC minutes mapped to each of the nine functions
Annual ITSC review of BCP and DR adequacy
ITSC-approved need-based access standards and procedures
IT and cybersecurity budget review by ITSC

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: D. Senior Management and IT Steering Committee

controls.title: Senior Management responsibilities for IT strategy execution and cyber posture
controls.prose: Senior Management must ensure execution of the Board-approved IT strategy, effective and efficient functioning of IT / information security and supporting infrastructure, IT risk management processes and a culture of IT risk awareness and cyber hygiene, a robust cybersecurity posture, and that IT contributes to productivity and efficiency.
controls.guidance: Evidence with Senior Management MIS on IT strategy execution, cyber hygiene programme reports and posture dashboards (for example patch latency and MFA coverage from para 194 metrics). Maxwell KPI series from report-audit-improvements can serve as posture evidence. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 19; Payments Bank Directions para 19; AIFI Directions para 19; Credit Information Company Directions para 19; NBFC Directions para 74 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
controls.category: Senior Management and IT Steering Committee
evidenceExpected: Senior Management MIS on IT strategy execution
Cyber hygiene and risk awareness programme reports
Cybersecurity posture dashboard

controls.title: IT Steering Committee meets at least quarterly
controls.prose: The bank must establish an IT Steering Committee with Senior Management representation from IT and business functions that meets at least quarterly.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the IT Steering Committee constitution, membership showing IT and business representation at Senior Management level, and minutes for the last four quarters. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 20; Payments Bank Directions para 20; AIFI Directions para 20; Credit Information Company Directions para 20; NBFC Directions para 75 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
controls.category: Senior Management and IT Steering Committee
evidenceExpected: IT Steering Committee constitution and membership
Minutes for the last four quarters

params.label: Minimum IT Steering Committee meeting frequency

controls.title: IT Steering Committee responsibilities
controls.prose: The IT Steering Committee must assist the ITSC in strategic IT planning, oversight of IT performance and aligning IT with business needs; oversee business continuity and DR processes; ensure a robust IT architecture meeting statutory and regulatory compliance; and periodically update the ITSC and MD / CEO on its activities.
controls.guidance: Map IT Steering Committee minutes to the four responsibilities and confirm periodic update notes to ITSC and MD / CEO exist. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 21; Payments Bank Directions para 21; AIFI Directions para 21; Credit Information Company Directions para 21; NBFC Directions para 76 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
controls.category: Senior Management and IT Steering Committee
evidenceExpected: IT Steering Committee terms of reference
Update notes to ITSC and MD / CEO

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: E. Information Security Committee

controls.title: Information Security Committee under ITSC oversight, headed from risk management
controls.prose: An Information Security Committee (ISC) must be formed under ITSC oversight to manage cyber / information security. The ITSC decides its constitution, which includes the CISO and representatives of business, IT and other functions; the ISC head must come from the risk management vertical. The ISC is responsible for developing information security / cybersecurity policies and implementing policies, standards and procedures so risks stay within risk appetite; approving and monitoring security projects and awareness initiatives; reviewing cyber incidents, IS audit observations, monitoring and mitigation; and periodically updating the ITSC and MD / CEO.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the ITSC decision constituting the ISC, membership showing the CISO and a chair from risk management (not IT), and ISC minutes reviewing incidents (link inc_ records), IS audit observations and VA/PT closure (para 161). An ISC chaired by the Head of IT is a finding. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 22; Payments Bank Directions para 22; AIFI Directions para 22; Credit Information Company Directions para 22; NBFC Directions para 77 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: ITSC decision on ISC constitution
ISC membership with chair from risk management and CISO as member
ISC minutes reviewing incidents, IS audit observations and mitigation
ISC updates to ITSC and MD / CEO

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: F. Head of IT Function

controls.title: Appoint a senior, technically competent Head of IT Function
controls.prose: The bank must appoint a sufficiently senior, technically competent and experienced official as Head of IT Function (CTO, CIO or equivalent nomenclature).
controls.guidance: Evidence with the appointment order and profile of the Head of IT. Record the role holder in details.json contacts (cto or cio role). Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 23; Payments Bank Directions para 23; AIFI Directions para 23; Credit Information Company Directions para 23; NBFC Directions para 78 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Appointment order of the Head of IT Function
Profile evidencing seniority and IT experience

controls.title: Head of IT responsibilities including DR setup and BCP strategy
controls.prose: The Head of IT Function is responsible for ensuring IT projects align with the IT policy and strategy, an effective IT organisational structure, and an effective DR setup and business continuity strategy / plan.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the Head of IT role description and the DR architecture and BCP owned by the Head of IT; DR effectiveness itself is tested under paras 165-174. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 24; Payments Bank Directions para 24; AIFI Directions para 24; Credit Information Company Directions para 24; NBFC Directions para 79 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Head of IT role description
DR setup and BCP strategy owned by the Head of IT

controls.title: Head of IT as first line of defence for IT controls and IT risk
controls.prose: As first line of defence, the Head of IT must ensure effective assessment, evaluation and management of IT controls and IT risk, including robust internal controls, to secure the bank's information assets and comply with internal policies and regulatory and legal requirements on IT.
controls.guidance: Evidence with first-line control self-assessments signed by the Head of IT and IT risk registers owned by IT. Maxwell static and runtime probe observations provide independent testing of those first-line controls. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 25; Payments Bank Directions para 25; AIFI Directions para 25; Credit Information Company Directions para 25; NBFC Directions para 80 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: First-line IT control self-assessment
IT risk register owned by the Head of IT

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: G. Chief Information Security Officer

controls.title: Senior CISO independent of the Head of IT, without business targets, adequately staffed and budgeted
controls.prose: A senior executive, preferably of General Manager rank or equivalent, must be designated CISO. The CISO must have no direct reporting relationship with the Head of IT Function and must not be given business targets. The bank must ensure the CISO has the requisite technical background, is appointed for a reasonable minimum term, has an office adequately staffed with technical expertise commensurate with business volume, technology adoption and complexity, and that the information security / cybersecurity budget reflects the current and emerging threat landscape.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the CISO appointment order (rank, term), the organisation chart showing no reporting line to the Head of IT, confirmation that the CISO's KRAs carry no business targets, CISO office headcount and skills, and the security budget. A dotted or solid line from CISO to CIO / CTO is a high-severity finding. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 26; Payments Bank Directions para 26; AIFI Directions para 26; Credit Information Company Directions para 26; NBFC Directions para 81 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: CISO appointment order with rank and term
Organisation chart showing CISO reporting line
CISO KRAs without business targets
CISO office staffing plan and security budget

params.label: Preferred minimum rank of the CISO

controls.title: Documented CISO role: strategy, enforcement, ITSC invitee, SOC and effective security solutions
controls.prose: The CISO's roles must be documented and at minimum cover: (1) driving cybersecurity strategy and ensuring compliance with regulatory / statutory instructions; (2) enforcing information asset protection policies and coordinating security issues internally and with external agencies; (3) being a permanent invitee to the ITSC and IT Steering Committee; (4) the CISO's office managing and monitoring the SOC and driving cybersecurity projects; and (5) ensuring security solutions function effectively. Sub-paragraphs 28(6) (reporting line) and 28(7) (quarterly review) are catalogued as separate controls.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the CISO charter or job description listing items (1)-(5), ITSC / IT Steering Committee invitations and minutes showing CISO attendance, and the SOC operating model placing SOC management under the CISO office. A charter missing any of the five roles, or a SOC run by IT operations without CISO oversight, is a finding. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 27; Payments Bank Directions para 27; AIFI Directions para 27; Credit Information Company Directions para 27; NBFC Directions para 82 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Documented CISO roles and responsibilities
ITSC and IT Steering Committee invitations and attendance
SOC management under the CISO office

controls.title: CISO reports directly to the Executive Director overseeing risk management
controls.prose: The CISO must report directly to the Executive Director or equivalent overseeing the risk management function.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the organisation chart and CISO appointment order showing a direct line to the risk-management Executive Director. A CISO reporting to the CRO below ED level without an equivalent-executive rationale, or to the Head of IT (see also para 27), is a high-severity finding; refresh-ctx re-checks the line on every CISO or ED change. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 27; Payments Bank Directions para 27; AIFI Directions para 27; Credit Information Company Directions para 27; NBFC Directions para 82 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Organisation chart showing CISO reporting line
CISO appointment order naming the Executive Director overseeing risk management

controls.title: CISO places a cybersecurity risk and preparedness review before the Board, RMCB or ITSC quarterly
controls.prose: The CISO must place a review of cybersecurity risks, arrangements and preparedness of the bank before the Board, the Risk Management Committee of the Board or the ITSC at least on a quarterly basis.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the quarterly cyber preparedness papers and the Board / RMCB / ITSC minutes recording them. report-audit-findings output can be the quarterly paper's evidence base. A quarter without a review is a finding; refresh-soc computes the next due date from the last minuted review and cisoBoardReviewFrequency. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 27; Payments Bank Directions para 27; AIFI Directions para 27; Credit Information Company Directions para 27; NBFC Directions para 82 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Quarterly cyber risk and preparedness review papers placed before Board, RMCB or ITSC
Board, RMCB or ITSC minutes recording each quarterly review

params.label: Minimum frequency of CISO cybersecurity review before Board, RMCB or ITSC

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: H. Information Technology Project Management

controls.title: Formally defined IT project management approach
controls.prose: The bank must follow a consistent, formally defined project management approach for IT projects that enables stakeholder participation and effective monitoring of project risks and progress.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the project management methodology and, for a sample of recent projects, risk logs and steering updates. probe-sdlc checks that the sdlc/policy.json project gates exist and are followed in repository history. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). controls.title: Enterprise architecture methodology for new or emerging technologies

Architecture review records for new technology adoptions

controls.title: Adopt new or emerging technology within risk appetite, securely and resiliently
controls.prose: Adoption of new or emerging technologies must be commensurate with the bank's risk appetite, aligned with business and IT strategy, and must enable creation, use and sharing of information in a secure and resilient way.
controls.guidance: Evidence with risk assessments for new technology adoptions (for example LLM-based agents, low-code platforms, public cloud services) signed against the risk appetite. probe-agent-graph, runtime-probe-harnesses and runtime-probe-sandboxes observations show whether agent tooling, harness permissions and sandbox isolation match the approved risk posture. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 30; Payments Bank Directions para 30; AIFI Directions para 30; Credit Information Company Directions para 30; NBFC Directions para 87 (Middle Layer and above). Security and resilience design review for the adoption

controls.title: Product approval and quality assurance for new IT business products
controls.prose: Any new IT application proposed as a business product (for customers, prospective customers, third parties or internal employees) must go through the prescribed product approval and quality assurance process.
controls.guidance: Evidence with product approval committee records and QA sign-off for each new customer- or employee-facing application release. probe-sdlc and probe-cicd-env confirm QA gates (runtime-probe-qa-env for the QA environment) exist before production deployment. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 31; Payments Bank Directions para 31; AIFI Directions para 31; Credit Information Company Directions para 31; NBFC Directions para 88 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Product approval committee record
QA sign-off before go-live

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: I. IT Architecture

controls.title: Security-by-design IT architecture reviewed annually by ITSC, with documented trade-offs
controls.prose: The IT architecture must be designed so security measures are always in place. The ITSC must review it at least annually and it must be upgraded as needed based on risk assessment in a phased manner. The bank must document any risk-cost or potential cost trade-off decisions in writing for supervisory assessment.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the current architecture document, the annual ITSC review minute and a trade-off register. probe-iac and probe-app-chart provide as-built evidence (segmentation, encryption, redundancy) to compare with the documented architecture; undocumented deviations are findings. Annual ITSC architecture review minute
Written register of risk-cost trade-off decisions

groups.title: Chapter III - Information Technology Governance and Oversight: J. IT Services Management

controls.title: IT Service Management framework for operational resilience including DR sites

Service catalogue including DR site services

controls.title: Service Level Management with segregation of duties
controls.prose: The bank must have a Service Level Management process for IT operations that maintains effective segregation of duties.

Segregation of duties matrix for IT operations

controls.title: Security classification of information assets by criticality (CIA)
controls.prose: The bank must identify and map the security classification of information assets in terms of confidentiality, integrity and availability, based on their criticality to operations.

evidenceExpected: Information asset inventory with CIA classification

controls.title: Avoid outdated and unsupported hardware and software; track EOS and AMC dates
controls.prose: To keep business operations running, the bank must avoid outdated and unsupported hardware or software and continuously monitor software End-of-Support dates and hardware Annual Maintenance Contract dates.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-appcontainers and runtime-probe-prod-env inventory OS, runtime and base-image versions and compare them against vendor EOS dates (for example end-of-life Kubernetes minor versions, unsupported JDK or Python runtimes, EOL database engines); probe-iac checks pinned engine versions. Any production component past EOS without an approved exception (para 59) is a high-severity finding. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 36; Payments Bank Directions para 36; AIFI Directions para 36; Credit Information Company Directions para 36; NBFC Directions para 92 (Middle Layer and above). Runtime version inventory compared with vendor EOS calendars
Exceptions for any EOS component

controls.title: Technology refresh plan before EOS
controls.prose: The bank must maintain a technology refresh plan to replace hardware and software in time, before they reach End-of-Support.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the refresh plan listing each component nearing EOS with a funded replacement date. impl-change-management tracks refresh initiatives; components within six months of EOS without a plan entry are findings. groups.title: Chapter IV - IT and Information Security Risk Management: A. Periodic Review of IT related Risks

controls.title: Risk management policy covers IT and cyber risk, reviewed annually by RMCB with ITSC
controls.prose: The bank's risk management policy must include IT-related risks, including cybersecurity risks, and the Risk Management Committee of the Board, in consultation with the ITSC, must review and update it at least annually.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the risk policy IT / cyber section and the RMCB minute (with ITSC consultation) from the last 12 months. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 38; Payments Bank Directions para 38; AIFI Directions para 38; Credit Information Company Directions para 38; NBFC Directions para 94 (Middle Layer and above). controls.category: Periodic Review of IT related Risks
evidenceExpected: Risk management policy section on IT and cyber risks
Annual RMCB review minute with ITSC consultation

groups.title: Chapter IV - IT and Information Security Risk Management: B. IT and Information Security Risk Management Framework

controls.title: IT and information security risk management framework
controls.prose: The bank must establish a robust IT and Information Security Risk Management Framework (the information security / cybersecurity framework may be separate from the IT risk framework) covering: a comprehensive information security function, internal controls and processes (including applicable insurance) reviewed periodically for efficacy; roles and responsibilities of stakeholders including third-party personnel, with role conflicts and accountability gaps identified and removed or managed; identification of critical information systems and fortification of their security environment; and systems, procedures and controls for secure storage, transmission and processing of data.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the framework document, the Board-approved list of critical information systems (used by para 151 and para 165 cadences), cyber insurance cover and control efficacy reviews. Maxwell uses the critical-system list to decide which applications/<app_id>/env files are in scope for half-yearly VA and DR drills. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 39; Payments Bank Directions para 39; AIFI Directions para 39; Credit Information Company Directions para 39; NBFC Directions para 95 (Middle Layer and above). controls.category: IT and Information Security Risk Management Framework
evidenceExpected: IT and information security risk management framework
List of critical information systems
Control efficacy reviews and cyber insurance cover
Role conflict and accountability gap analysis

groups.title: Chapter IV - IT and Information Security Risk Management: C. Risk Identification, Assessment, and Documentation

controls.title: Per-asset risk assessment guided by security standards
controls.prose: Risk assessment of each in-scope information asset must be guided by appropriate security standards or IT control frameworks.
controls.guidance: Evidence with risk assessments naming the framework used (ISO 27005, NIST SP 800-30, CIS) per asset. Maxwell soc risk records (rsk_) should cite the asset and the framework basis. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). evidenceExpected: Asset-level risk assessments referencing the standard used

controls.title: Staff and service providers comply with security and acceptable-use policies
controls.prose: All staff and service providers must comply with the information security and acceptable-use policies applicable to them.
controls.guidance: Evidence with signed acceptable-use acknowledgements for employees and vendor personnel, and policy compliance exceptions logs. refresh-vendor-ctx records which vendors have signed the bank's security schedule. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). evidenceExpected: Signed acceptable-use acknowledgements
Vendor security policy compliance attestations

controls.title: Annual review of security infrastructure and policies; tackle phishing and spoofing
controls.prose: The bank must review its security infrastructure and security policies at least annually in light of its own experience and emerging threats, and take steps to tackle cyber-attacks including phishing and spoofing and mitigate their effects.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the annual security architecture and policy review report and anti-phishing / anti-spoofing measures (DMARC under para 120, takedown services under para 148). runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks email authentication records for the bank's domains. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 42; Payments Bank Directions para 42; AIFI Directions para 42; Credit Information Company Directions para 42; NBFC Directions para 98 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Annual security infrastructure and policy review report
Anti-phishing and anti-spoofing measures in place

controls.title: Inherent risk identification factors
controls.prose: When identifying and assessing inherent risks the bank must consider the technologies adopted, alignment with business and regulatory requirements, organisational culture, and internal and external threats.
controls.guidance: Check the risk methodology lists these four factors and that recent assessments score them. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 43; Payments Bank Directions para 43; AIFI Directions para 43; Credit Information Company Directions para 43. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Risk methodology covering technology, alignment, culture and threats

controls.title: Categorise inherent riskiness (low to very high)
controls.prose: Depending on inherent risk, the bank must classify its riskiness as low, moderate, high or very high (or a similar scale), factoring in the riskiness of each business component.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the inherent risk rating output per business component. Maxwell maps these ratings to soc risk severity when importing. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 44; Payments Bank Directions para 44; AIFI Directions para 44; Credit Information Company Directions para 44. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Inherent riskiness classification per business component

controls.title: Control evaluation factors including threat intelligence and information sharing
controls.prose: When evaluating controls, the bank must factor in Board oversight, policies, processes, cyber risk architecture, experienced resources, training and culture; threat intelligence gathering and analysis relative to the banking sector; information sharing with peer banks, IDRBT, RBI and CERT-In; preventive, detective and corrective controls; vendor management; and incident management and response.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the control evaluation methodology and records of threat-intelligence subscriptions (IB-CART, CERT-In advisories) considered in the evaluation. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 45; Payments Bank Directions para 45; AIFI Directions para 45; Credit Information Company Directions para 45. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Control evaluation methodology
Threat intelligence and information sharing arrangements referenced in the evaluation

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: A. Inventory Management of Information Assets

controls.title: Up-to-date information asset inventory with business criticality
controls.prose: The bank must maintain an up-to-date inventory of information assets, including business and customer data, business applications, supporting IT infrastructure, key personnel and facilities (hardware, software, network devices and services), indicating each asset's business criticality. The bank may set its own criteria for critical assets.
controls.guidance: Maxwell evidences inventory completeness by comparing applications/<app_id>/ (repos, images, env) and refresh-metastore catalogues with what runtime probes discover: cloud resources from runtime-probe-prod-env, container images from runtime-probe-appcontainers and data stores from runtime-probe-datapipeline. Discovered assets missing from the inventory (shadow IT) or lacking a criticality rating are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 46; Payments Bank Directions para 46; AIFI Directions para 46; Credit Information Company Directions para 46; UCB Directions para 21 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Information asset inventory with criticality ratings
Reconciliation of inventory against discovered cloud, container and data assets
Criteria used to identify critical assets

controls.title: Classify data by sensitivity
controls.prose: The bank must classify data and information according to its own information classification / sensitivity criteria.
controls.guidance: probe-schemas and refresh-metastore check that datasets and fields holding customer PII, account, card and KYC data carry classification tags (for example restricted / confidential / internal). Unclassified tables containing Aadhaar, PAN or card numbers are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 47; Payments Bank Directions para 47; AIFI Directions para 47; Credit Information Company Directions para 47; UCB Directions para 19 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Data classification scheme
Classification tags on data stores and schemas

controls.title: Enterprise data dictionary
controls.prose: The bank must maintain an enterprise data dictionary to enable data sharing between applications and systems and a common understanding of data.
controls.guidance: refresh-metastore reconciles the metastore catalogue (company-profile/<c>/sdlc/metastore.json) with the bank's data dictionary; tables or event schemas without dictionary entries are gaps. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 48; Payments Bank Directions para 48; AIFI Directions para 48; Credit Information Company Directions para 48; NBFC Directions para 100 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Enterprise data dictionary with data types, structures and security restrictions

controls.title: Protect data inside and outside the network by sensitivity
controls.prose: The bank must manage and protect data within and outside its network and organisational boundaries, considering how data is stored, transmitted, processed, accessed and used and the risk it faces given its sensitivity.
controls.guidance: probe-iac and runtime-probe-datapipeline check encryption, access policies and public exposure of storage (object stores, databases, message queues) in line with classification; data flows to partners and SaaS are compared with the metastore lineage. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 49; Payments Bank Directions para 49; AIFI Directions para 49; Credit Information Company Directions para 49; UCB Directions para 20 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Data handling standard per classification
Storage and transfer controls evidenced for restricted data

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: B. Data Leak Prevention Strategy

controls.title: Comprehensive data loss / leakage prevention strategy
controls.prose: The bank must develop a comprehensive data loss / leakage prevention strategy for sensitive and confidential business and customer data, covering data on endpoints, data in transmission, and data in servers and other digital stores whether online or offline.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the DLP strategy and tool coverage across endpoint, email, web and storage channels. runtime-probe-datapipeline checks for unmasked sensitive data in non-production copies and public buckets; probe-iac checks storage public-access blocks. Coverage gaps on any of the three data states are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 50; Payments Bank Directions para 50; AIFI Directions para 50; Credit Information Company Directions para 50; UCB Directions para 124 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: DLP strategy document
DLP tool coverage for endpoints, network egress and data stores
DLP incident reports

controls.title: Equivalent data leak prevention at vendor-managed facilities
controls.prose: The bank must ensure similar data leak prevention arrangements at vendor-managed facilities.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx records whether each vendor handling bank data has contractual DLP obligations and evidence (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 scope, DLP attestations). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 51; Payments Bank Directions para 51; AIFI Directions para 51; Credit Information Company Directions para 51. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Vendor contracts with DLP clauses
Vendor DLP attestations or audit reports

controls.title: Bank as owner protects customer data wherever it is held, across the lifecycle
controls.prose: As owner of customers' personal and sensitive data, the bank must preserve its confidentiality, integrity and availability whether stored or in transit internally or with third-party vendors, ensure confidentiality of custodial information is never compromised, and implement systems and processes across the data lifecycle for this.
controls.guidance: Evidence with data lifecycle controls (collection, storage, sharing, retention, disposal) and vendor data-protection clauses. Map to DPDP Rules 2025 security safeguards; runtime-probe-datapipeline samples retention, masking and access on customer data stores. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 52; Payments Bank Directions para 52; AIFI Directions para 52; Credit Information Company Directions para 52; UCB Directions para 22 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Customer data lifecycle controls
Vendor data protection clauses and assurance
Data retention and secure disposal records

controls.title: Remote manage, wipe and lock mobile devices and laptops
controls.prose: The bank must implement controls to remotely manage, wipe and lock mobile devices, including laptops.
controls.guidance: Evidence with MDM / UEM enrolment coverage and a tested remote-wipe record. Maxwell cannot probe endpoints directly; record as document-review observations from MDM exports. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 53; Payments Bank Directions para 53; AIFI Directions para 53; Credit Information Company Directions para 53. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: MDM or UEM enrolment coverage report
Remote wipe and lock test record

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: C. Data Migration Controls

controls.title: Data migration policy ensuring integrity, completeness, audit trails and stage sign-offs
controls.prose: The bank must have a data migration policy defining a systematic migration process that ensures data integrity, completeness and consistency, including audit trails of migration activity and sign-offs from business users and application owners at each stage.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the migration policy and, for recent migrations (core banking upgrades, cloud moves), reconciliation reports and stage sign-offs. runtime-probe-datapipeline checks row-count and checksum reconciliation jobs where migrations run through pipelines. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 54; Payments Bank Directions para 54; AIFI Directions para 54; Credit Information Company Directions para 54; NBFC Directions para 99 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Data migration policy
Migration reconciliation reports and audit trails
Stage-wise business and application owner sign-offs

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: D. Preventing Execution of Unauthorised Software

controls.title: Centralised inventory of authorised and unauthorised software; whitelisting
controls.prose: The bank must maintain an up-to-date centralised inventory of authorised and unauthorised software and may whitelist authorised applications, software, libraries and other components.
controls.guidance: Software inventory evidence includes a Software Bill of Materials per production image and application (CycloneDX or SPDX generated in CI), which also covers libraries. probe-cicd-env checks SBOM generation, runtime-probe-appcontainers compares running images with the inventory, and execute-scr flags unapproved dependencies. The Directions do not name SBOMs; SBOM is Maxwell's recommended implementation of the library-level inventory (compare SEBI CSCRF GV.SC.S5). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 55; Payments Bank Directions para 55; AIFI Directions para 55; Credit Information Company Directions para 55; UCB Directions para 27 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Centralised authorised software inventory
SBOM per production image or application
Application or library whitelist where implemented

controls.title: Control and block unauthorised software installation on endpoints, servers, mobile and cloud
controls.prose: The bank must control installation of software on its information systems including PCs, laptops, workstations, servers, mobile devices and cloud environments, and must be able to block, prevent and identify installation and execution of unauthorised software.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-appcontainers and probe-app-chart check admission controls (signed images only, allowed registries, no privileged or host-mount containers); probe-iac checks cloud policies restricting marketplace or unapproved images. Endpoint application control is evidenced by EDR / allow-listing reports. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 56; Payments Bank Directions para 56; AIFI Directions para 56; Credit Information Company Directions para 56; UCB Directions para 26 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Software installation control policy and tooling
Container admission and image signing policy
Reports of blocked unauthorised software

controls.title: Monitor vendor patches and CERT-In advisories; emergency patching for exploited critical vulnerabilities
controls.prose: The bank must continuously monitor patch releases from vendors / OEMs and advisories from CERT-In and similar agencies and apply security patches expeditiously per its patch management policy. Where patches address critical vulnerabilities that are actively exploited or widely reported, the bank must be able to deploy them expeditiously through its emergency patch process.
controls.guidance: cve-enrichment ties KEV-listed and CERT-In advisory CVEs to components found by runtime-probe-appcontainers, runtime-probe-prod-env and execute-scr. A known-exploited critical vulnerability open beyond the bank's emergency patch timeline is a critical finding; the Directions set no fixed day count, so the SLA table applies. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 57; Payments Bank Directions para 57; AIFI Directions para 57; Credit Information Company Directions para 57. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Patch and advisory monitoring records (OEM, CERT-In)
Emergency patch management procedure
Evidence of expedited deployment for actively exploited vulnerabilities

controls.title: Exception policy with justification, duration, approval and senior periodic review
controls.prose: The bank must have a policy specifying justification and duration of exceptions, the granting process, approving authority and periodic review of granted exceptions by senior officers who understand their business and technical context.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the exception register (id, control, justification, expiry, approver, last review). Maxwell treats expired or never-reviewed exceptions as findings and links active exceptions to soc control records to suppress duplicates. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 58; Payments Bank Directions para 58; AIFI Directions para 58; Credit Information Company Directions para 58. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Exception management policy
Exception register with expiry dates and senior reviews

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: E. Physical and Environmental Controls

controls.title: Physical and environmental protection of DC and DR sites
controls.prose: The bank must implement appropriate physical and environmental controls to secure locations of critical assets, including primary data centres and DR sites, against natural and man-made threats.
controls.guidance: Evidence with DC / DR site audit reports, co-location provider certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2, Uptime tier) and cloud region attestations. For cloud-hosted workloads, refresh-vendor-ctx records the CSP physical security attestations. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 59; Payments Bank Directions para 59; AIFI Directions para 59; Credit Information Company Directions para 59; NBFC Directions para 101 (Middle Layer and above); UCB Directions para 30 (Level I and above).
evidenceExpected: DC and DR physical security audit reports
Co-location or CSP physical and environmental attestations

controls.title: Monitor environmental control breaches and service availability alerts
controls.prose: The bank must monitor breaches of environmental controls including temperature, water, smoke, access alarms, service availability alerts (power, telecom, servers) and access logs.
controls.guidance: Evidence with BMS / DCIM alert configuration and sample alert tickets; for cloud, provider health notifications integrated into the SOC. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 60; Payments Bank Directions para 60; AIFI Directions para 60; Credit Information Company Directions para 60; UCB Directions para 31 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Environmental monitoring alert configuration
Sample environmental alert tickets and access logs

controls.title: Geographically separated DC and DR sites
controls.prose: Data centre and DR sites must be geographically well separated so that a threat tied to one location does not affect both.
controls.guidance: probe-iac and runtime-probe-prod-env record the regions and zones used for primary and DR (for example AWS ap-south-1 Mumbai and ap-south-2 Hyderabad, or Azure Central India and South India). DR in another availability zone of the same region is a finding for critical systems. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 61; Payments Bank Directions para 61; AIFI Directions para 61; Credit Information Company Directions para 61; NBFC Directions para 102 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: DC and DR location details with seismic / flood zone analysis
Cloud region configuration for primary and DR

controls.title: E-surveillance at DC and DR sites
controls.prose: DC and DR sites must be under the necessary e-surveillance.
controls.guidance: Evidence with CCTV / e-surveillance coverage reports and footage retention from site audits or provider attestations. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 62; Payments Bank Directions para 62; AIFI Directions para 62; Credit Information Company Directions para 62; NBFC Directions para 103 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: E-surveillance coverage and retention evidence for DC and DR

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: F. Capacity Management

controls.title: Systems support business functions and availability of all delivery channels
controls.prose: Information systems and infrastructure must be able to support business functions and keep all service delivery channels available.
controls.guidance: Evidence with channel availability reports (internet banking, mobile, UPI, ATM, branch). runtime-probe-prod-env checks autoscaling limits, resource saturation and redundancy for customer-facing services. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 63; Payments Bank Directions para 63; AIFI Directions para 63; Credit Information Company Directions para 63; NBFC Directions para 107 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Channel availability reports
Capacity and redundancy configuration for delivery channels

controls.title: Annual capacity assessment aligned with peak trends and projected needs
controls.prose: At least annually the bank must proactively assess IT capacity requirements, ensuring capacity planning across components, services, resources and supporting infrastructure reflects past peak usage, current requirements and projected needs under the IT strategy.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the annual capacity plan using peak data (for example salary-day, festival-season UPI peaks) and the ITSC review under para 19(8). Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 64; Payments Bank Directions para 64; AIFI Directions para 64; Credit Information Company Directions para 64; NBFC Directions para 108 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Annual IT capacity assessment with peak usage trends and projections

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: G. Secure Configuration

controls.title: Documented baseline security configurations for all device categories, reviewed periodically
controls.prose: The bank must document and apply baseline security configurations to all device categories (endpoints, mobile devices, operating systems, databases, applications, network and security devices and systems) across the lifecycle from conception to deployment, and review them periodically.
controls.guidance: probe-iac, probe-app-chart and runtime-probe-appcontainers compare infrastructure-as-code, Helm charts and running containers against CIS Benchmarks and the bank's hardening baselines (non-root containers, read-only filesystems, encrypted volumes, IMDSv2, no default credentials). Drift from baseline in production is a finding. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 65; Payments Bank Directions para 65; AIFI Directions para 65; Credit Information Company Directions para 65; UCB Directions para 109 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Hardening baselines per device and platform category
Configuration compliance scan results
Periodic baseline review record

controls.title: Periodic review of firewall, switch and security device configurations and patch levels
controls.prose: The bank must periodically evaluate critical devices such as firewalls, switches and security devices, including configuration and patch levels, across its network including data centres, third-party hosted sites and shared infrastructure.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter reviews security groups, NACLs, WAF and firewall policies for any-any rules and stale entries; probe-iac checks firewall rule definitions. Evidence the periodic rule review sign-off. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 66; Payments Bank Directions para 66; AIFI Directions para 66; Credit Information Company Directions para 66. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Firewall and network device configuration review reports
Device patch level report
Rule-base review sign-off

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: H. Network Management and Security

controls.title: Only authorised, time-limited, audited network access; responsibility with bank officials
controls.prose: Only authorised access to the bank's networks is permitted, granted through a defined process with strict time limits that is consistently followed and periodically audited. Responsibility for such networks must rest with bank officials.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access and runtime-probe-network-perimeter check VPN, bastion and cloud network access grants for expiry, approval tickets and named bank owners. Standing vendor network access without expiry is a finding. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 67; Payments Bank Directions para 67; AIFI Directions para 67; Credit Information Company Directions para 67. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Network access request and approval records with expiry
Periodic network access audit report
Named bank owners for each network

controls.title: Up-to-date organisation-level network architecture diagram
controls.prose: The bank must maintain an up-to-date organisation-wide network architecture diagram including wired and wireless networks.
controls.guidance: Compare the diagram with VPCs, subnets, peering and transit gateways discovered by probe-iac and runtime-probe-network-perimeter; undocumented segments are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 68; Payments Bank Directions para 68; AIFI Directions para 68; Credit Information Company Directions para 68. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Current network architecture diagram
Reconciliation with discovered network topology

controls.title: Centralised inventory of authorised network-connected devices
controls.prose: The bank must maintain an up-to-date centralised inventory of authorised devices connected to its network inside or outside its premises, and may automate network discovery and management.
controls.guidance: Evidence with NAC / CMDB device inventory and discovery scan reconciliation. Cloud workloads are reconciled by runtime-probe-prod-env. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 69; Payments Bank Directions para 69; AIFI Directions para 69; Credit Information Company Directions para 69; UCB Directions para 105 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Authorised device inventory
Network discovery reconciliation report

controls.title: Appropriate network device configuration assessed periodically
controls.prose: All network devices must be configured appropriately, and the bank must periodically assess whether configurations deliver the desired level of network security.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter and probe-iac check load balancer TLS policies, security group rules, open management ports and logging on network devices. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 70; Payments Bank Directions para 70; AIFI Directions para 70; Credit Information Company Directions para 70; UCB Directions para 33 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Network device configuration assessments

controls.title: Secure wireless LANs, access points and client access
controls.prose: The bank must implement appropriate controls to secure wireless LANs, wireless access points and wireless client access systems.
controls.guidance: Evidence with WLAN configuration (WPA3-Enterprise / 802.1X, rogue AP detection). Outside Maxwell's cloud probe reach; record as document-review observations. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 71; Payments Bank Directions para 71; AIFI Directions para 71; Credit Information Company Directions para 71; UCB Directions para 35 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: WLAN security configuration
Rogue access point detection reports

controls.title: Only compliant, identified devices get network connectivity
controls.prose: The bank must identify authorised hardware and mobile devices (laptops, phones, tablets) on the network and provide connectivity only when they meet its security requirements.
controls.guidance: Evidence with NAC / device posture check configuration and conditional access policies (device compliance required for SSO). runtime-probe-identity-access checks identity-provider conditional access rules. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 72; Payments Bank Directions para 72; AIFI Directions para 72; Credit Information Company Directions para 72. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: NAC or device posture enforcement configuration
Conditional access policies requiring compliant devices

controls.title: Automatically detect and block unauthorised device connections
controls.prose: The bank must have mechanisms to automatically identify and block unauthorised device connections to its network.
controls.guidance: Evidence with NAC blocking logs and alerting rules for unknown MAC / device certificates. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 73; Payments Bank Directions para 73; AIFI Directions para 73; Credit Information Company Directions para 73. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Unauthorised device detection and blocking logs

controls.title: Detect and remedy unusual activity in systems, servers, network devices and endpoints
controls.prose: The bank must have mechanisms to detect and remedy unusual activities in systems, servers, network devices and endpoints.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-prod-env checks that cloud threat detection (GuardDuty, Defender for Cloud, Security Command Center) and EDR are enabled and routed to the CSOC; disabled detectors in production accounts are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 74; Payments Bank Directions para 74; AIFI Directions para 74; Credit Information Company Directions para 74; UCB Directions para 134 (Level III and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Anomaly detection tooling coverage (EDR, cloud threat detection, NDR)
Sample detections with remediation tickets

controls.title: SOPs for all major IT activities including connecting devices
controls.prose: The bank must establish SOPs for all major IT activities, including connecting devices to the network.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the SOP library index and version history. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 75; Payments Bank Directions para 75; AIFI Directions para 75; Credit Information Company Directions para 75. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: SOP library covering major IT activities including device connection

controls.title: Multi-layered boundary defence and real-time traffic filtering
controls.prose: Boundary defences must be multi-layered, with properly configured firewalls, proxies, DMZ perimeter networks and network-based IPS and IDS, and robust real-time filtering of inbound and outbound traffic.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter tests internet exposure (open ports, management interfaces, WAF presence on customer-facing endpoints, egress filtering from workloads) and probe-iac checks DMZ subnet design, NAT / egress proxies and IDS/IPS or cloud network firewall deployment. Workloads with unrestricted egress to 0.0.0.0/0 are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 76; Payments Bank Directions para 76; AIFI Directions para 76; Credit Information Company Directions para 76; UCB Directions para 106 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Perimeter architecture with DMZ, firewalls, proxies and IDS/IPS
Egress filtering configuration
External attack surface scan results

controls.title: Public-facing IT infrastructure handles IPv6 traffic
controls.prose: The bank must enable its public-facing IT infrastructure to handle IPv6 traffic.
