controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter resolves AAAA records and tests IPv6 reachability and TLS on public endpoints (internet banking, mobile APIs, corporate website); probe-iac checks dual-stack load balancers. IPv6 endpoints must carry the same WAF and firewall policies as IPv4. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 77; Payments Bank Directions para 77; AIFI Directions para 77; Credit Information Company Directions para 77; NBFC Directions para 18(4) (Base Layer Rs 500 crore and above); UCB Directions para 108 (Level II and above). Base Layer NBFCs, HFCs and NBFC-P2P platforms are in applicability because the NBFC Directions carry this obligation for the Base Layer tier of Rs 500 crore and above; a Base Layer entity below Rs 500 crore is out of scope for this control and should be recorded not-applicable with its asset size as the reason.
evidenceExpected: AAAA records and IPv6 reachability tests for public endpoints
Dual-stack load balancer and WAF configuration

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: I. Application Security Life Cycle

controls.title: Information security in every stage of the application life cycle
controls.prose: The bank must build information security into all stages of the application life cycle.
controls.guidance: probe-sdlc checks sdlc/policy.json defines security gates for requirements, design, build, test, release and operations, and that repository history shows them followed (threat model artefacts, SAST/SCA in CI, security sign-off on release). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 78; Payments Bank Directions para 78; AIFI Directions para 78; Credit Information Company Directions para 78. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Secure SDLC policy with stage-wise security gates
Evidence of gates in repositories and pipelines

controls.title: Secure coding practices for in-house and co-developed applications
controls.prose: The bank must implement secure coding practices for applications developed internally or collaboratively.
controls.guidance: execute-scr runs secure code review (SAST, secrets, dependency and IaC scanning) on repositories in applications/<app_id>/repos and emits SARIF; probe-cicd-env checks those scans block merges on high findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 79; Payments Bank Directions para 79; AIFI Directions para 79; Credit Information Company Directions para 79. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Secure coding standard
SAST, secret and dependency scan results per repository
Developer secure coding training records

controls.title: Security requirements specified from initial stages of development or acquisition
controls.prose: Besides business functionality, the bank must clearly specify security requirements for access control, authentication, transaction authorisation, data integrity, activity logging, audit trail, session management, security event tracking and exception handling from the initial and ongoing stages of development, acquisition and implementation.
controls.guidance: Evidence with security requirement templates in BRDs / epics and traceability to tests. execute-scr samples implementation of session management, authorisation checks and audit logging in code against OWASP ASVS. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 80; Payments Bank Directions para 80; AIFI Directions para 80; Credit Information Company Directions para 80; UCB Directions para 142 (Level III and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Security requirements in design documents for sampled applications
Traceability from security requirements to tests

controls.title: Segregated development, test and production environments
controls.prose: The bank must properly segregate development, test and production environments.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks separate cloud accounts / subscriptions / projects and networks per environment; runtime-probe-devtest-env and runtime-probe-qa-env confirm no network paths or shared credentials into production and no production data copies without masking. Shared Kubernetes clusters across dev and prod without hard isolation are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 81; Payments Bank Directions para 81; AIFI Directions para 81; Credit Information Company Directions para 81; UCB Directions para 110 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Environment segregation architecture
Network and identity isolation evidence between environments
Access lists showing developers lack production write access

controls.title: Threat modelling, secure coding, standards-aligned security testing and secure deployment
controls.prose: The software development process must be guided by threat modelling, follow secure coding practices, include security testing aligned with global standards, and ensure secure deployment.
controls.guidance: probe-sdlc looks for threat models for critical applications, probe-cicd-env for DAST / SAST / container scanning and deployment integrity (signed artefacts, protected branches, no manual production pushes), and probe-agent-graph for threat models of AI agent workflows. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 82; Payments Bank Directions para 82; AIFI Directions para 82; Credit Information Company Directions para 82; UCB Directions para 111 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Threat models for critical applications
Security test reports aligned to OWASP ASVS or equivalent
Secure deployment pipeline controls

controls.title: Address vulnerabilities proactively using OWASP baselines and defence-in-depth
controls.prose: Development practices must proactively address vulnerabilities using best practices and baselines such as OWASP and apply defence-in-depth for layered security.
controls.guidance: execute-scr maps findings to OWASP Top 10 / ASVS and OWASP LLM Top 10 for AI features; probe-app-chart checks layered controls (WAF, network policies, pod security). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 83; Payments Bank Directions para 83; AIFI Directions para 83; Credit Information Company Directions para 83; UCB Directions para 143 (Level III and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: OWASP-based secure development baseline
Layered security design evidence

controls.title: Application security assessments broader than OWASP Top 10
controls.prose: Application security assessments must be comprehensive and not limited to the OWASP Top 10, referring to other recognised standards and guidelines as appropriate.
controls.guidance: Check assessment scopes reference OWASP ASVS, MASVS for mobile, API Security Top 10 and business-logic testing, not only the Top 10. Assessment reports scoped only to OWASP Top 10 are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 84; Payments Bank Directions para 84; AIFI Directions para 84; Credit Information Company Directions para 84. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Application security assessment scope documents referencing ASVS, MASVS, API Security or equivalent

controls.title: Application security testing across lifecycle in production-like environments
controls.prose: The bank must periodically test the security of web and mobile applications across their lifecycle (pre-implementation, post-implementation and after changes) in an environment closely resembling or replicating production.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-qa-env checks QA parity with production (versions, configuration, WAF); probe-cicd-env checks security tests run on each release. Releases without a post-change security test are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 85; Payments Bank Directions para 85; AIFI Directions para 85; Credit Information Company Directions para 85; UCB Directions para 115 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Application security test reports per release
Evidence of test environment parity with production

controls.title: Containerised, encrypted business apps on mobile devices with remote wipe
controls.prose: The bank must, as applicable, install containerised apps on mobile phones for exclusive business use, encrypted and separated from other data and apps, and be able to remotely wipe the container so its data becomes unreadable.
controls.guidance: Evidence with MDM app-protection / work-profile policies and a remote-wipe test record. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 86; Payments Bank Directions para 86; AIFI Directions para 86; Credit Information Company Directions para 86. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Mobile application containerisation policy
Remote wipe of container test record

controls.title: Evaluate new technologies for security before use in critical systems
controls.prose: The bank must adequately evaluate new technologies against existing and evolving security threats, and introduce them for critical systems only after the IT and security teams reach reasonable comfort and maturity.
controls.guidance: Evidence with security evaluations before adoption (for example of generative-AI coding assistants, agent frameworks, MCP servers). probe-agent-graph and runtime-probe-harnesses verify guardrails, tool permissions and human approval steps before agentic tools touch critical systems. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 87; Payments Bank Directions para 87; AIFI Directions para 87; Credit Information Company Directions para 87; UCB Directions para 144 (Level III and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Security evaluation of new technology before critical-system use
IT and security team sign-off

controls.title: Vendor maintenance and support enforced by formal agreements
controls.prose: The bank must ensure software vendors provide maintenance and support for applications and enforce this through formal agreements.
controls.guidance: refresh-vendor-ctx records support and maintenance terms and end-of-support dates for each vendor-supplied application. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 88; Payments Bank Directions para 88; AIFI Directions para 88; Credit Information Company Directions para 88; NBFC Directions para 104 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Software maintenance and support agreements

controls.title: Source code or escrow for critical applications including updates
controls.prose: The bank must obtain source code for all critical applications from vendors; where that is not possible it must use source code escrow or other arrangements that adequately mitigate vendor default risk, with all product updates and programme fixes included in escrow.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the list of critical vendor applications (core banking, payment switch, treasury, LOS) and for each the source code custody or escrow agreement and the latest escrow deposit verification covering the current version. Escrow deposits older than the production version are findings. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 89; Payments Bank Directions para 89; AIFI Directions para 89; Credit Information Company Directions para 89; NBFC Directions para 105 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Source code custody or escrow agreements for critical applications
Escrow deposit verification covering the production version

controls.title: Consider source code audits of critical business applications
controls.prose: For critical business applications the bank may consider source code audits by professionally competent personnel or service providers.
controls.guidance: Where the bank holds source, execute-scr can perform or supplement the audit; record the independent auditor's report otherwise. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 90; Payments Bank Directions para 90; AIFI Directions para 90; Credit Information Company Directions para 90; UCB Directions para 141 (Level III and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Source code audit reports for critical applications

controls.title: Vendor certificate that application is free of known vulnerabilities, malware and covert channels, renewed on material change
controls.prose: The bank must obtain a certificate or written confirmation from the developer or vendor that the application is free of known vulnerabilities, malware and covert channels, and obtain it again whenever material code changes, including upgrades, occur. Material changes are significant code modifications that could affect functionality, security or performance, excluding routine maintenance (minor bug fixes, performance optimisation, updates not altering core functions, security posture or compliance status); materiality may be agreed with the vendor and must be decided through risk assessment.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the certificate per vendor application version and the materiality risk assessment for each upgrade. Maxwell cross-checks the certificate claim against execute-scr, SBOM-based CVE matching (cve-enrichment) and container scans; known CVEs in a certified version are findings against both this control and vendor management. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 91; Payments Bank Directions para 91; AIFI Directions para 91; Credit Information Company Directions para 91; NBFC Directions para 106 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Vendor certificates of no known vulnerabilities, malware or covert channels per version
Materiality risk assessments for code changes
Independent scan results supporting the certificate

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: J. Maintenance, Monitoring, and Analysis of Audit Logs

controls.title: Audit logging and trails for systems that can access or affect critical data
controls.prose: Every IT application or system that can access or affect critical or sensitive information must have the necessary audit logging capabilities and provide audit trails.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks cloud audit logging (CloudTrail / Activity Log / Cloud Audit Logs incl. data events for sensitive stores), probe-app-chart and execute-scr check application audit events, runtime-probe-datapipeline checks database audit logging. Critical systems without audit trails are high findings. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 92; Payments Bank Directions para 92; AIFI Directions para 92; Credit Information Company Directions para 92; NBFC Directions para 109 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
controls.category: Maintenance, Monitoring, and Analysis of Audit Logs
evidenceExpected: Audit logging configuration for critical applications, databases and cloud control planes

controls.title: Validated log settings capturing uniquely identifiable log records
controls.prose: The bank must implement, and periodically validate, settings capturing appropriate logs and audit trails for every device, system software and application, with minimum information to uniquely identify each log such as date, timestamp, source and destination addresses and other relevant packet, event or transaction elements.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-prod-env samples log records to verify timestamp (NTP-synchronised, see CERT-In Dir-i), user / service identity, source and destination IP, action and outcome fields; missing source IP or identity in authentication and transaction logs is a finding. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 93; Payments Bank Directions para 93; AIFI Directions para 93; Credit Information Company Directions para 93; UCB Directions para 151 (Level III and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
controls.category: Maintenance, Monitoring, and Analysis of Audit Logs
evidenceExpected: Log field standard
Periodic log configuration validation results

controls.title: Audit trails meet business, legal and regulatory needs and support forensics and non-repudiation
controls.prose: Audit trails must satisfy business, regulatory and legal requirements and be detailed enough to support audits, serve as digital forensic evidence and assist dispute resolution including non-repudiation.
controls.guidance: The Directions state no retention period; retention must satisfy other applicable law. For Indian entities that means at least CERT-In Directions 2022 (180 days, within India) and DPDP Rules 2025 (one year for personal data processing logs), plus any longer RBI record retention the bank applies. probe-iac and runtime-probe-datapipeline check log bucket retention, immutability (object lock) and India-region storage; record the adopted retention as the soc parameter logRetentionDays. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 94; Payments Bank Directions para 94; AIFI Directions para 94; Credit Information Company Directions para 94; NBFC Directions para 110 (Middle Layer and above); UCB Directions para 126 (Level II and above).
controls.category: Maintenance, Monitoring, and Analysis of Audit Logs
evidenceExpected: Log retention and integrity standard referencing legal requirements
Immutable log storage configuration
Sample audit trail reconstructing a disputed transaction

params.label: Audit log retention adopted by the bank to meet business, legal and regulatory requirements (no period stated in the Directions; CERT-In requires 180 days)

controls.title: Regular monitoring of audit trails and system logs
controls.prose: The bank must have a system to regularly monitor audit trails and system logs to detect, understand or recover from unauthorised activity or attacks.
controls.guidance: Evidence with SIEM ingestion coverage for critical systems and review records for high-risk logs. runtime-probe-prod-env checks log sources are forwarded to the SIEM. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 95; Payments Bank Directions para 95; AIFI Directions para 95; Credit Information Company Directions para 95; NBFC Directions para 111 (Middle Layer and above); UCB Directions para 150 (Level III and above).
controls.category: Maintenance, Monitoring, and Analysis of Audit Logs
evidenceExpected: SIEM log source coverage for critical systems
Log review and alert triage records

controls.title: Consult stakeholders on log collection scope, frequency and storage
controls.prose: Before finalising scope, frequency and storage of log collection, the bank must consult all stakeholders.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the logging standard approval record showing consultation of business, IT, security, audit, legal and compliance. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 96; Payments Bank Directions para 96; AIFI Directions para 96; Credit Information Company Directions para 96; UCB Directions para 149 (Level III and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
controls.category: Maintenance, Monitoring, and Analysis of Audit Logs
evidenceExpected: Log management standard with stakeholder consultation record

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: K. Patch, Vulnerability and Change Management

controls.title: Documented change and patch management policy
controls.prose: The bank must have documented change and patch management policies and procedures ensuring: business impact of implementing or not implementing a patch or change is assessed; patches and changes are applied and reviewed securely and on time with approvals; every application or data change is justified by genuine business need, documented and subject to robust change management; and failed changes or patch deployments can be recovered.
controls.guidance: probe-sdlc checks change records for impact assessment, approval and rollback plans; probe-cicd-env checks branch protection, required approvals and automated rollback in deployment pipelines. Production changes without an approved change record (for example direct kubectl edits) are findings; impl-change-management tracks remediation. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 97; Payments Bank Directions para 97; AIFI Directions para 97; Credit Information Company Directions para 97; NBFC Directions para 112 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Change and patch management policy
Change records with impact assessment, approvals and rollback plans
Pipeline approval and rollback configuration

controls.title: Risk-based patching strategy with inventory of components needing patches
controls.prose: The bank must adopt a documented, risk-based strategy for maintaining an inventory of IT components requiring patches, identifying applicable patches and applying them promptly to minimise vulnerable systems and exposure time.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-appcontainers, runtime-probe-prod-env and cve-enrichment compute per-component patch latency; severity-based targets come from the bank's patch policy or the SLA table where it sets none. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 98; Payments Bank Directions para 98; AIFI Directions para 98; Credit Information Company Directions para 98. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Risk-based patch strategy
Inventory of patchable components
Patch latency report

controls.title: Track patch status for internet-connected endpoints, servers, databases and middleware
controls.prose: The bank must have systems to identify, track, manage and monitor patch status for OS and applications on internet-connected end-user devices, and for server OS, databases, applications, middleware and other relevant systems.
controls.guidance: Evidence with patch compliance dashboards; runtime probes report node OS, database engine and middleware versions against latest security releases. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 99; Payments Bank Directions para 99; AIFI Directions para 99; Credit Information Company Directions para 99; UCB Directions para 41 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Patch compliance dashboards for endpoints and servers
Database and middleware patch status

controls.title: Configuration management and baselines ensure integrity of changes
controls.prose: Changes to business applications, supporting technology, service components and facilities must be managed through robust configuration management processes and baselines to preserve change integrity.
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks that infrastructure is managed as code with drift detection; runtime-probe-prod-env reports drift between deployed state and IaC / GitOps source. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 100; Payments Bank Directions para 100; AIFI Directions para 100; Credit Information Company Directions para 100; UCB Directions para 114 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Configuration management database or GitOps source of truth
Drift detection reports

controls.title: Root cause of detected incidents and patching of exploited vulnerabilities
controls.prose: As part of threat mitigation, the bank must determine the root cause of any detected incident and apply the patches needed to address the vulnerabilities.
controls.guidance: Link each inc_ record in the soc ledger to its RCA and the closing change or patch; incidents closed without RCA are findings. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 101; Payments Bank Directions para 101; AIFI Directions para 101; Credit Information Company Directions para 101. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Incident RCA reports
Patches or changes implemented to address incident root cause

controls.title: Secure configuration and patching of access points between VLANs, LAN/WAN and partner networks
controls.prose: The bank must periodically evaluate access device configurations and patch levels so that all access points and nodes between DC VLANs, LAN / WAN interfaces, and the bank's network and external, partner, vendor and service-provider networks are securely configured.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter reviews VPC peering, VPN / Direct Connect / ExpressRoute and partner API gateway configurations (for example NPCI, card network and fintech partner links) for least-privilege routing and current patch levels. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 102; Payments Bank Directions para 102; AIFI Directions para 102; Credit Information Company Directions para 102. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Interconnection point configuration reviews
Patch levels of devices at network boundaries and partner links

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: L. User Access Control / Management

controls.title: Access only on valid business need
controls.prose: Access to information assets is allowed only where a valid business need exists.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access compares IAM, directory and database grants with the ITSC-approved access standards (para 19(9)) and joiner-mover-leaver records; unused or unjustified entitlements are findings. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 103; Payments Bank Directions para 103; AIFI Directions para 103; Credit Information Company Directions para 103; NBFC Directions para 113 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Access request approvals with business justification
Periodic user access recertification

controls.title: Supervise and log privileged users with periodic activity review
controls.prose: Personnel with elevated system access must be closely supervised, with all their system activity logged and periodically reviewed.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access checks privileged session recording (PAM) and cloud admin activity logging; evidence the periodic review sign-off. Break-glass accounts used without post-use review are findings. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 104; Payments Bank Directions para 104; AIFI Directions para 104; Credit Information Company Directions para 104; NBFC Directions para 114 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Privileged session logs or recordings
Periodic privileged activity review reports

controls.title: Protect data at rest and in transit for access within and outside the network
controls.prose: The bank must provide secure access to assets and services from within and outside its network, protecting data at rest (for example with encryption where the device supports it) and in transit (for example VPN or other secure protocols).
controls.guidance: probe-iac checks encryption at rest for disks, object stores, databases and backups (KMS-managed keys) and TLS enforcement; runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks TLS versions and plaintext listeners on external endpoints. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 105; Payments Bank Directions para 105; AIFI Directions para 105; Credit Information Company Directions para 105; UCB Directions para 120 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Encryption at rest configuration
TLS / VPN enforcement for remote and external access

controls.title: Protect credentials, tokens and access profiles from leakage and attack
controls.prose: The bank must protect user access credentials such as user-ids, authentication information, tokens and access profiles against leakage and attacks.
controls.guidance: execute-scr scans repositories and container images for hard-coded secrets; probe-cicd-env checks pipeline secrets are masked and short-lived (OIDC federation); runtime-probe-appcontainers checks for secrets in environment variables. Any exposed live credential is a critical finding. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 106; Payments Bank Directions para 106; AIFI Directions para 106; Credit Information Company Directions para 106. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Secret scanning results for code, images and pipelines
Credential vault usage evidence
Token lifetime and rotation configuration

controls.title: No admin rights on end-user devices; time-bound need-to-know access
controls.prose: The bank must disallow administrative rights on end-user workstations, PCs and laptops, and grant access rights on a need-to-know basis for a specific duration through an established process.
controls.guidance: Evidence with endpoint local admin reports and just-in-time elevation records; probe-dev-env checks developer workstation baselines where managed. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 107; Payments Bank Directions para 107; AIFI Directions para 107; Credit Information Company Directions para 107; UCB Directions para 43 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Endpoint local administrator exceptions report
Time-bound access elevation records

controls.title: Centralised authentication and authorisation with strong passwords, least privilege and SoD
controls.prose: The bank must implement centralised authentication and authorisation for accessing and administering applications, operating systems, databases, network and security devices and connectivity points (local or remote), enforcing a strong password policy, least privilege and separation of duties.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access checks SSO / IdP federation for consoles, Kubernetes, databases and bastions, local account sprawl, password policy settings and SoD conflicts (for example the same identity able to create and approve payments or deploy and approve changes). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 108; Payments Bank Directions para 108; AIFI Directions para 108; Credit Information Company Directions para 108; UCB Directions para 145 (Level III and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Centralised IAM / directory integration coverage
Password policy configuration
Least privilege and SoD conflict analysis

controls.title: Risk-based 2FA/MFA, mandatory MFA for privileged users of critical systems and activities
controls.prose: Based on risk assessment the bank must implement two-factor or multi-factor authentication, including mandatory MFA for privileged users of critical information systems and of critical activities.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access verifies MFA enforcement (not merely availability) for cloud root and admin roles, IdP admins, PAM, VPN, Kubernetes cluster-admin and database admin paths on critical systems, and for critical activities such as payment release. Any privileged path on a critical system without MFA is a critical finding. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 109; Payments Bank Directions para 109; AIFI Directions para 109; Credit Information Company Directions para 109; NBFC Directions para 115 (risk-based MFA for privileged users; the word mandatory is absent). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: MFA enforcement policies for privileged users
List of critical systems and critical activities with MFA coverage
Risk assessment for non-privileged MFA scope

params.label: Mandatory MFA for privileged users of critical information systems and critical activities

controls.title: Centralised allow, manage, log and monitor privileged access to critical systems
controls.prose: The bank must implement appropriate (for example centralised) systems and controls to allow, manage, log and monitor privileged, superuser and administrative access to critical servers, operating systems, databases, applications, middleware and network devices.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access checks privileged access is brokered through PAM or just-in-time elevation with session logging, and that direct SSH / RDP / database admin access bypassing PAM is blocked by network rules (runtime-probe-network-perimeter). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 110; Payments Bank Directions para 110; AIFI Directions para 110; Credit Information Company Directions para 110; UCB Directions para 46 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: PAM coverage of critical systems
Privileged session logs
Network controls preventing PAM bypass

controls.title: Limit invalid logons and deactivate dormant accounts
controls.prose: The bank must implement controls to minimise invalid logon attempts and deactivate dormant accounts.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access checks lockout thresholds and finds accounts and access keys unused beyond the bank's dormancy period that remain active. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 111; Payments Bank Directions para 111; AIFI Directions para 111; Credit Information Company Directions para 111. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Account lockout configuration
Dormant account deactivation report

params.label: Inactivity period after which accounts are deactivated (bank-defined; not stated in the Directions)

controls.title: Monitor abnormal logon patterns
controls.prose: The bank must monitor any abnormal change in logon patterns.
controls.guidance: Evidence with SIEM / IdP risk detections (impossible travel, unusual hours, brute force) and triage records; runtime-probe-identity-access checks IdP risk policies are enabled. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 112; Payments Bank Directions para 112; AIFI Directions para 112; Credit Information Company Directions para 112. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Abnormal logon detection rules
Triage records for logon anomalies

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: M. Controls on Teleworking

controls.title: Secure teleworking: secure remote access, MFA to critical systems, remote device identification, data protection
controls.prose: In teleworking the bank must: ensure systems used and remote access from alternate locations to environments hosting its information assets are secure; implement MFA for enterprise logical access to critical systems; identify all remote-access devices connected to its systems; and secure data shared or presented while teleworking.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-identity-access checks MFA and device compliance on VPN / ZTNA and VDI; runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks remote access gateways for exposure and patch level; probe-dev-env checks developer remote environments (cloud IDEs, codespaces) do not hold production credentials. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 113; Payments Bank Directions para 113; AIFI Directions para 113; Credit Information Company Directions para 113; NBFC Directions para 116 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Remote access architecture (VPN, ZTNA, VDI)
MFA enforcement for remote access to critical systems
Inventory of remote-access devices
Telework data handling controls (DLP, screen watermarking)

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: N. Authentication Framework for Customers

controls.title: Customer authentication with positive identity verification and bank authenticity across channels
controls.prose: The bank must implement an authentication framework that positively verifies customers' identity when they access its services and lets customers verify the bank's authenticity, across all delivery channels.
controls.guidance: execute-scr reviews login, device binding, OTP and step-up logic in internet and mobile banking code; runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks certificate validity, HSTS and certificate pinning indicators on customer endpoints; bank authenticity measures include verified sender IDs (DLT-registered SMS headers), verified domains and in-app authenticity checks. Map customer channel requirements to RBI digital payment security controls where applicable. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 114; Payments Bank Directions para 114; AIFI Directions para 114; Credit Information Company Directions para 114; UCB Directions para 122 (Level II and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Customer authentication framework per channel
Mechanisms for customers to verify bank authenticity
Authentication test results for internet and mobile banking

controls.title: Bank as identity provider for customer access to partner systems
controls.prose: The bank must act as identity provider for identifying and authenticating customers accessing partner systems, using secure authentication technologies.
controls.guidance: For open-banking, fintech and co-lending partner integrations and third-party APIs, execute-scr and runtime-probe-network-perimeter check that partners rely on bank-issued OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect tokens (PKCE, short-lived tokens, mTLS or signed requests for server-to-server APIs) rather than collecting bank credentials. Partners capturing customer net-banking credentials is a high finding. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 115; Payments Bank Directions para 115; AIFI Directions para 115; Credit Information Company Directions para 115. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Federation design for partner access (OIDC / OAuth)
Partner API authentication configuration
Partner integration security review

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: O. Secure Mail and Messaging Systems

controls.title: Secure mail and messaging against spoofing, look-alike domains, malicious content and spam; partners likewise
controls.prose: The bank must implement secure mail and messaging with measures against email spoofing and look-alike domain abuse, protection against malicious attachments and links, and spam filtering, and must require partners and vendors to do the same.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter checks SPF, DKIM and DMARC on bank sending domains, MX gateway protections and look-alike domain monitoring; refresh-vendor-ctx records partner email security obligations. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 116; Payments Bank Directions para 116; AIFI Directions para 116; Credit Information Company Directions para 116; UCB Directions para 52 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Email gateway protections (attachment sandboxing, URL rewriting, spam filtering)
Look-alike domain monitoring
Partner and vendor email security requirements

controls.title: Email server specific controls
controls.prose: The bank must document and implement email-server-specific controls.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the email server hardening standard (open relay disabled, TLS enforced, admin MFA) and configuration review. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 117; Payments Bank Directions para 117; AIFI Directions para 117; Credit Information Company Directions para 117; UCB Directions para 53 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Email server hardening standard and review

controls.title: Control permissible email attachment types
controls.prose: The bank must control which attachment types are permitted in email.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the gateway attachment policy blocking executable and macro-enabled types. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 118; Payments Bank Directions para 118; AIFI Directions para 118; Credit Information Company Directions para 118. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Email attachment type policy configuration

controls.title: DMARC on bank email domains; urge third parties to implement
controls.prose: The bank must implement DMARC for its email domains and impress on vendors, partners and other third parties to implement similar solutions to mitigate spoofing.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter resolves _dmarc records for every sending and parked domain in details.json; policy p=none or missing DMARC on a sending domain is a finding, and parked domains should publish p=reject with null SPF. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 119; Payments Bank Directions para 119; AIFI Directions para 119; Credit Information Company Directions para 119; UCB Directions para 54 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: DMARC records at enforcement for bank domains
DMARC aggregate report monitoring
Communications to third parties on DMARC

params.label: DMARC policy expected on bank email domains (Directions require DMARC; enforcement level is bank-set)

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: P. Removable Media

controls.title: Removable media not permitted by default
controls.prose: By default the bank must not permit removable devices and media in the banking environment unless specifically authorised for a defined use and duration.
controls.guidance: Evidence with endpoint device control policy default-deny and the register of authorised exceptions with expiry. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 120; Payments Bank Directions para 120; AIFI Directions para 120; Credit Information Company Directions para 120; UCB Directions para 55 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Default-deny removable media policy configuration
Authorised removable media exception register

controls.title: Removable media and BYOD policy with secure erasure
controls.prose: The bank must define and implement a policy restricting and securing removable media and BYOD on all device categories (workstations, PCs, laptops, mobile devices, servers) and ensure secure erasure of data on such media after use.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the removable media / BYOD policy and media sanitisation records. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 121; Payments Bank Directions para 121; AIFI Directions para 121; Credit Information Company Directions para 121; UCB Directions para 56 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Removable media and BYOD policy
Secure erasure records

controls.title: Limit media types and information transferable
controls.prose: The bank must limit the media types and information that can be copied to or from removable devices.
controls.guidance: Evidence with device control rules limiting media classes and DLP rules restricting classified data transfer. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 122; Payments Bank Directions para 122; AIFI Directions para 122; Credit Information Company Directions para 122. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Device control and DLP rules for removable media

controls.title: Malware scan of removable media before access
controls.prose: The bank must scan removable media for malware before granting read / write access.
controls.guidance: Evidence with endpoint protection configuration for on-insert scanning. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 123; Payments Bank Directions para 123; AIFI Directions para 123; Credit Information Company Directions para 123; UCB Directions para 57 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: On-insert malware scanning configuration

controls.title: Consider centralised removable media policies via AD or endpoint management
controls.prose: The bank should consider implementing centralised whitelist / blacklist / restriction policies for removable media through Active Directory or endpoint management systems.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the GPO / MDM policy objects applied centrally. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 124; Payments Bank Directions para 124; AIFI Directions para 124; Credit Information Company Directions para 124; UCB Directions para 146 (Level III and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Centralised removable media policy objects

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: Q. Third-Party Arrangements

controls.title: Vendor risk assessment and proportionate controls for concentration, conflicts, SPOF, compliance, availability and supply chain
controls.prose: The bank must have a vendor risk assessment process and controls proportionate to assessed risk and materiality to mitigate concentration risk, eliminate or address conflicts of interest, mitigate single points of failure, comply with legal and regulatory requirements and standards protecting customer data, provide high availability for uninterrupted customer service, and manage supply chain risks effectively.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). refresh-vendor-ctx maintains company-profile/<c>/vendors/<vendor_id>.json with criticality tier, concentration (for example a single CSP or single core banking vendor hosting DC and DR), certifications and supply chain dependencies; SBOM-derived component suppliers feed supply chain risk. Vendors without a current risk assessment are findings. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 125; Payments Bank Directions para 125; AIFI Directions para 125; Credit Information Company Directions para 125; NBFC Directions para 117 (Middle Layer and above). No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Vendor risk assessment methodology and completed assessments
Third-party register with criticality and concentration analysis
Single point of failure and exit analysis for critical vendors

controls.title: Bank accountable for security assurance in outsourced and partner arrangements
controls.prose: The bank is accountable for appropriate management of, and assurance on, security risks in outsourced and partner arrangements.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). Evidence with the assurance plan per critical vendor (audit rights exercised, SOC 2 / ISO reports reviewed, VA/PT reports received) and the named bank owner. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 126; Payments Bank Directions para 126; AIFI Directions para 126; Credit Information Company Directions para 126; UCB Directions para 71 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Third-party security assurance plan and results
Named bank owner per arrangement

controls.title: Evaluate need to outsource critical processes; select vendors on comprehensive risk assessment
controls.prose: The bank must carefully evaluate the need to outsource critical processes and select vendors and partners on the basis of comprehensive risk assessment.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). Evidence with outsourcing need assessments and vendor selection risk assessments for critical processes. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 127; Payments Bank Directions para 127; AIFI Directions para 127; Credit Information Company Directions para 127. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Outsourcing need assessment for critical processes
Vendor selection risk assessment

controls.title: Ongoing due diligence, oversight and management of vendors and partners
controls.prose: The bank must regularly conduct effective due diligence, oversight and management of third-party vendors, service providers and partners.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). refresh-vendor-ctx re-checks vendor certifications, breach disclosures and financial condition; overdue periodic due diligence on a critical vendor is a finding. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 128; Payments Bank Directions para 128; AIFI Directions para 128; Credit Information Company Directions para 128. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Periodic vendor due diligence records
Vendor performance and security review minutes

controls.title: Policies to evaluate, approve, review and monitor vendor risk and materiality
controls.prose: The bank must establish policies and procedures to evaluate, assess, approve, review, control and monitor the risks and materiality of all vendor and outsourcing activities.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). Evidence with the third-party risk management policy and materiality criteria. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 129; Payments Bank Directions para 129; AIFI Directions para 129; Credit Information Company Directions para 129. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Third-party risk management policy with materiality criteria

controls.title: Demonstrate service provider compliance with Indian laws and regulations
controls.prose: The bank must ensure, and be able to demonstrate, that each service provider complies with all regulatory and legal requirements of the country.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). Evidence with vendor compliance attestations (CERT-In incident reporting and log retention, DPDP processor obligations, data localisation) held in vendors/<vendor_id>.json. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 130; Payments Bank Directions para 130; AIFI Directions para 130; Credit Information Company Directions para 130. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Vendor legal and regulatory compliance attestations

controls.title: Agreements with right to audit by the bank and RBI inspection rights
controls.prose: The bank must enter into agreements with service providers that, among other things, provide the bank a right to audit and RBI or persons it authorises a right to inspect.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). refresh-vendor-ctx records whether each contract contains bank audit and RBI inspection clauses; a critical vendor contract without them is a high finding. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 131; Payments Bank Directions para 131; AIFI Directions para 131; Credit Information Company Directions para 131. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Contract clauses granting bank audit rights and RBI inspection rights

controls.title: RBI access to information resources consumed, even if hosted off-premises
controls.prose: The bank must ensure RBI has online or in-person access to all information resources it consumes, and must make that information accessible to RBI officials on request even where the infrastructure is not on bank premises.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). Evidence with contract clauses and a tested supervisory access procedure for cloud and SaaS providers. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 132; Payments Bank Directions para 132; AIFI Directions para 132; Credit Information Company Directions para 132. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Contract clauses and procedure ensuring RBI access to off-premises information resources

controls.title: Comply with data location and cross-border data movement requirements
controls.prose: The bank must adhere to legal and regulatory requirements on the geographical location of infrastructure and cross-border movement of data.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). probe-iac and runtime-probe-prod-env check cloud regions and replication targets for payment and customer data (RBI payment data storage localisation, DPDP Rules 2025 cross-border conditions); refresh-metastore records data residency per dataset. Payment system data replicated outside India beyond permitted processing is a critical finding. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 133; Payments Bank Directions para 133; AIFI Directions para 133; Credit Information Company Directions para 133. Not carried into the NBFC Directions. No direct equivalent in the UCB Directions.
evidenceExpected: Data residency map per dataset and system
Cloud region and replication configuration
Legal assessment of cross-border transfers

controls.title: Vet vendor personnel with background checks, NDAs and security compliance agreements
controls.prose: The bank must satisfy itself about the credentials of vendor and third-party personnel accessing or managing its critical assets; background checks, non-disclosure and security policy compliance agreements are mandatory for all third-party service providers.
controls.guidance: Paragraphs 126-135 apply only to IT / cybersecurity third-party arrangements outside the RBI (Commercial Banks - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025; material IT outsourcing is governed there (and earlier by the 2023 IT outsourcing Master Direction mapped below, repealed 28 Nov 2025 and kept only as a historical crosswalk). Evidence with vendor personnel background verification confirmations, signed NDAs and security undertakings; runtime-probe-identity-access lists third-party identities with access to critical systems for sampling. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 134; Payments Bank Directions para 134; AIFI Directions para 134; Credit Information Company Directions para 134; UCB Directions para 74 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: Background verification evidence for vendor personnel on critical assets
Signed NDAs and security compliance agreements

controls.title: Cybersecurity controls maintained by third-party ATM Switch ASPs
controls.prose: Where the bank manages its ATM switch ecosystem through shared services of a third-party ATM Switch Application Service Provider, it must ensure the ASP implements and maintains the controls in these Directions on unauthorised software (57-59), environmental controls (60-61), network management (69-71, 73-77), secure configuration (66-67), ASLC (79, 80, 82-84, 88), patch / vulnerability and change management (86, 99, 101-103), user access (106, 107, 112, 113), data leak prevention (51), audit logs (94, 96), incident response (164), advanced threat defence (144-145) and forensics (211).
controls.guidance: Applies only to banks using a shared ATM switch ASP. refresh-vendor-ctx records the ASP and the evidence for each referenced control group (ASP audit reports, VA/PT reports, CSOC reports). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 135; Payments Bank Directions para 135; UCB Directions para 83 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: ASP control compliance matrix against the referenced paragraphs
ASP audit and assurance reports

controls.title: ASP controls embedded in contract and scoped to the ATM switch and payment IT ecosystem
controls.prose: The paragraph 136 controls must be written into the contract with the third-party switch ASP and apply to the ASP's IT ecosystem (physical infrastructure, hardware, software, reconciliation systems, network interfaces, security solutions, HSMs, middleware and associated people, processes, systems and data) providing ATM switch or other payment system services to the bank.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the ASP contract schedule listing the controls and scope. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 136; Payments Bank Directions para 136; UCB Directions para 84 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.
evidenceExpected: ASP contract schedule incorporating paragraph 136 controls and scope

controls.title: Baseline contractual controls mandated on ATM Switch ASPs
controls.prose: Contracts with ATM switch ASPs must mandate baseline controls including: changing default passwords and no trivial passwords; centralised IAM with strong passwords, risk-based 2FA/MFA, least privilege and SoD; privileged user management for critical servers and devices; network segregation; firewall rules blocking unidentified outbound connections and reverse TCP shells; disabling remote connections from outside machines to the switch network; IP tables restricting SWIFT and ATM switch access to authorised systems; software integrity of switch applications; masking of development and test data; secure coding certification and tested architecture for new products and upgrades with assurance to the bank / RBI on request; source code audits of critical applications with assurance of no malicious code; robust change management with test cases, approvals, deployment and rollback plans; database security event and backend access monitoring; log generation and capture including user action audit logs for forensics; alerts on log setting changes; incident management and BCP/DR responsibility even when the ASP itself outsources, with timely incident notification to the bank; periodic VA/PT with reports and compliance shared on request and prompt remediation; a written incident response procedure; a CSOC with log collection, SIEM correlation and threat updates; and PCI-DSS and PCI-SSF compliance as applicable.
controls.guidance: Evidence with the ASP contract clause-by-clause mapping to the 24 baseline controls and the latest assurance (VA/PT report, PCI-DSS AoC, CSOC report) for each. Missing incident notification or VA/PT sharing clauses are high findings because they block the bank's own DAKSH reporting and VA/PT oversight. Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 137; Payments Bank Directions para 137; UCB Directions para 85 (Level I and above). Not carried into the NBFC Directions.

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: R. Cryptographic Controls

controls.title: Strong, non-deprecated cryptography compliant with law and regulation
controls.prose: Key lengths, algorithms, cipher suites and protocols used in transmission channels, data processing and authentication must be strong. The bank must adopt internationally accepted, published standards that are not deprecated or shown to be insecure or vulnerable, with configurations compliant with extant laws and regulatory instructions.
controls.guidance: runtime-probe-network-perimeter scans external and internal TLS endpoints (TLS 1.2+ only, no RC4/3DES/CBC-SHA1 suites, RSA 2048+ or ECDHE, valid chains); probe-iac checks KMS key specs, rotation and HSM use for PIN / card keys; execute-scr flags weak hashing (MD5 / SHA-1 for integrity or passwords) and hard-coded keys; probe-schemas checks sensitive fields are encrypted or tokenised. Maintain a cryptographic inventory with a deprecation plan for weak suites and post-quantum readiness. Comply-or-explain for foreign bank branches (paragraph 4). Equivalent obligations in the sibling 2026 Directions: SFB Directions para 139; Payments Bank Directions para 139; AIFI Directions para 135; Credit Information Company Directions para 135; NBFC Directions para 118 (Middle Layer and above); UCB Directions para 25 (Level I and above).

controls.prose: To prevent unauthorised modification, the bank must ensure there is no manual intervention in, or manual modification of, data transferred between processes or applications in respect of critical applications.

controls.prose: For critical information systems and systems in the DMZ with a customer interface, VA must be conducted at least once every six months and PT at least once every 12 months. For non-critical systems a risk-based approach decides whether and how often VA/PT is done.

controls.prose: After implementation of an IT project or upgrade, VA/PT must be performed on the production environment. If PT must unavoidably be done in a test environment, its version and configuration must resemble production and any deviation must be documented and approved by the ISC.

groups.title: Chapter V - Baseline Cybersecurity and Resilience Requirements: Y. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery

controls.title: BCP and DR policy based on best practice such as ISO 22301, updated on major developments
controls.prose: The BCP and DR policy must adopt best practices (for example ISO 22301) to reduce the likelihood or impact of disruptive incidents and maintain business continuity, and must be updated based on major developments and risk assessments.

controls.title: BCP/DR designed for rapid, secure recovery of critical operations after cyber-attacks within RTO
controls.prose: BCP and DR capabilities must support resilience objectives and enable rapid recovery and secure resumption of critical operations, including key cybersecurity controls, after cyber-attacks or other incidents within recovery time objectives while keeping processes and data secure.

controls.title: Report cyber incidents on DAKSH within six hours of detection and notify CERT-In

Housing Finance Companies are kept in applicability: the six-hour reporting obligation binds them under the NBFC Directions, and only the recipient may differ because HFCs are supervised by NHB. groups.title: Chapter VIII - Repeal and Other Provisions: A. Repeal and Saving

controls.title: Repeal of the 2016 Cyber Security Framework and IT Governance instructions, with saving
controls.prose: With these Directions, existing directions, instructions and guidelines on the Cybersecurity Framework and IT Governance for Commercial Banks are repealed, as communicated by circular DoS.CO.PPG.66/11.01.005/2026-27 of 31 July 2026; this covers the Cyber Security Framework in Banks (2 June 2016) and the Master Direction on IT Governance, Risk, Controls and Assurance Practices (7 November 2023) for these banks, and the sibling Directions repeal the corresponding instructions for SFBs, PBs, UCBs, AIFIs, NBFCs and CICs. Actions taken under repealed instructions remain governed by them, approvals granted continue under these Directions, and rights, liabilities, penalties and proceedings are not affected (paragraph 231). The Directions add to, and do not derogate from, other laws and regulations (paragraph 232), and RBI's interpretation is final and binding (paragraph 233).
controls.guidance: Informational control for crosswalking: refresh-ctx should mark soc control records keyed to rbi-cyber-security-framework-2016 and rbi-it-governance-md-2023 as superseded for entities covered by the 2026 Directions (append superseding records, never delete), carrying forward open findings by remapping regulatoryRefs to the equivalent paragraph-number control (e.g. rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026:182). The exact list of repealed circulars is in the DoS.CO.PPG.66 circular, which was not fetched verbatim in this run; maintainer verification needed before relying on the named instruments. Equivalent repeal paragraphs: SFB Directions para 229; Payments Bank Directions para 229; AIFI Directions para 224; Credit Information Company Directions para 224; NBFC Directions para 155; UCB Directions para 180 (Level I and above).
evidenceExpected: Mapping of repealed 2016 / 2023 control references to 2026 paragraphs
Superseding soc control records
